accuracy.evidence: Goal features follow the SMART convention (specific, measurable, achievable/realistic, time frame) and the IB PYP PSPE identity outcome for this age (set goals, plan, monitor and adjust). Research claims are stated as the literature does: Locke and Latham (specific, difficult goals outperform 'do your best'), Gollwitzer (implementation intentions as if–then plans), Harkin et al. 2016 meta-analysis (progress monitoring, especially recorded, aids goal attainment). Lab numbers check: 80 + 70 = 150 = 2 × 75 (on track), + 30 = 180 < 225 (behind by 45).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips: vague wishes ('be good at swimming', 'a bit better'), dream-size or too-soon goals ('like an Olympic star', 'by tomorrow', 20 books), no time frame ('one day'), believing bigger is always better, having no plan for obstacles ('try really hard', 'hope'), checking only at the deadline, reading one slow week as failure, and giving up the goal when the plan is what needs to change.

lab_distinct.evidence: Every activity is specific to setting and running a personal goal: sharpening a vague goal with three SMART slots and live check marks, a goal-size dial with too easy / stretch / too big zones, obstacle-to-if–then-plan matching, a cumulative progress chart against a plan line, and choosing the right adjustment. Breaking Tasks into Steps (flagsteps) orders job steps and Habits and Motivation (flaghabit) builds habit loops; neither has a goal dial, plan line or if–then matching, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner turns a wish into a checkable goal, discovers that the best size is a stretch, prepares if–then plans, sees on the chart exactly when progress falls behind plan, and practises the review-and-adjust step on three different causes (wrong time, weak sub-skill, goal too big). This covers all three evidence statements: state a specific goal with a timeframe, describe steps, review and adjust.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: the vague goal 'get better at swimming', 'as many as possible: 20' for goal size, 'you failed week 2' when 80 + 70 is exactly on plan, and 'give up the goal' when the plan is not working.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with nine distinct m= messages: unmeasurable 'better', too much too soon, no stretch, effort is not a plan, hoping is not planning, being stuck is not a reason to quit, repeating the same practice keeps the mistake, feelings versus real numbers, and waiting for the deadline.

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK 2.3 (limit 6.5) and adult text at FK 6.5 (limit 9.5). Examples are everyday for ages 9 to 11 (swimming, reading, keepy-ups, piano, times tables). Canvas text is in short phrases; option tiles are under ten words.

no_filler.evidence: Passes the filler regex and 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs cover wish versus goal, stretch size, if–then plans and tracking, and adjusting; adult paragraphs cover curriculum and terms, research, named mistakes, and the lab. Each lab step teaches a different part of the goal cycle.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of every step before and after Show me: the goal card and three check tiles fit at 390 px, the dial track and its labels are readable, the four if–then tiles stack without overlap, chart bars and totals are labelled, and the problem card and fix tiles wrap cleanly.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes and there are no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (slot options, −/+ 1 book, each if–then plan, Log week, each fix) and the canvas aria-label states the result after each move, for example 'Total 180, plan 225. Behind plan by 45 pages.'
